assumptions: A sponsor or CRO has an approved neurology protocol whose local endpoint operations are not adequately served.
A qualified clinic and investigators will enter the proposed master-services and study work-order structure.
The targeted signals can be collected at home with an acceptance rate that supports the pricing.
All clinical judgment, safety decisions, and regulated roles remain with appropriately qualified study personnel.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A named protocol pipeline, sponsor or CRO budget-owner interviews, an executed clinic-investigator agreement, documented regulatory roles, pilot acceptance and repeat rates, and fully loaded economics across qualification, labor, support, devices, insurance, and payment timing.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Treating local participant operations and signal-quality custody as a sponsor-accepted deliverable identifies a real missing layer between decentralised-trial software and protocol-grade neurological endpoints.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Missing or rejected endpoints can delay expensive studies, so the pain can be severe, but no sponsor interview, active protocol, rejection baseline, budget, or willingness to buy a Poland-focused node is evidenced.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Setup fees plus accepted participant-week pricing align revenue with usable output, yet qualified labor, devices, travel, privacy, validation, insurance, support, and long acceptance cycles could absorb the proposed margin.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Neurology studies needing home endpoints in Central Europe form a clear niche, but the addressable study pipeline, endpoint mix, participant density, and sponsor demand are entirely unquantified.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Global CROs, eClinical specialists, device vendors, and established investigator networks already bundle qualification, logistics, and sponsor access; the candidate has no exclusive clinic network or validated endpoint advantage.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful protocol-grade node could extend to additional neurological signals, studies, sponsors, cohorts, and nearby countries, though each extension may require fresh validation and oversight.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Accepted-data histories, operating procedures, and investigator relationships could compound, but the proposed contracts are nonexclusive, the relationships are not yet held, and sponsors can switch to larger qualified vendors.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Neuroscience and data-science skills fit endpoint QA, but the founder lacks clinical authority, participant access, sponsor relationships, study appointments, and evidence of a proprietary technical capability.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Regulatory recognition of decentralised trial elements supports the direction, while continuing sponsor, investigator, consent, and clinical-oversight duties prevent an easy software-only adoption wave.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: CRO vendor qualification and sponsor study planning are concentrated routes to meaningful contracts, but they are slow, trust-intensive, and inaccessible here without a secured investigator or clinic partnership.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Clinical quality, sensitive data, protocol deviations, device calibration, insurance, participant support, and qualified staffing make this difficult to launch part-time, and multiple independent gatekeepers control every study.

highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the offer to one sponsor-specified, non-diagnostic endpoint and secure a clinic-led paid pilot in which the sponsor supplies the protocol and devices and the venture is accountable only for pre-defined operational QA milestones.
main_structural_strength: Pricing against accepted endpoint output aligns the service with a costly sponsor outcome and could turn operational signal quality into a measurable learning loop.
primary_score_limiter: The business has no evidenced study pipeline or contracted clinical access and must clear sponsor qualification, investigator, ethics, privacy, and staffing gates before it can deliver anything.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Established CROs and decentralised-trial vendors already possess sponsor qualification systems and global device logistics, while some neurological endpoints cannot validly move into the home.
